text: 85 year old female, found on the floor of her bathroom by the home health aide this morning. She says she slipped getting out of the tub and fell, pain's an eight out of ten in the right hip, right leg is shortened and externally rotated.
facts: slipped getting out of the tub and fell
right leg is shortened and externally rotated

text: she was totally fine at dinner, then around nine i heard a thump and found her on the floor next to the bed, she says she just lost her balance and fell
speaker: daughter
notes: Fall dispatch, no stroke-like words: 'fine at dinner' and 'found her on the floor' give no stroke.lkw / onset_witnessed (§4c). Nested relay of the patient's words -> patient.

text: Sixty-two year old male, type one diabetic with an insulin pump, wife says he was fine at ten when she went to bed, she found him like this at six. BGL 38. We pushed D10, 150 mils IV at 0612, recheck is 142 and he's alert and oriented now.
notes: Hypoglycemia: 'fine at ten' is not stroke.lkw on a non-stroke call without stroke-like words (§4c).

text: Dispatched as a fall but it's not mechanical. Seventy-four yom, wife watched his right arm just go limp at the dinner table at 1915. Right facial droop, right arm drifts, right leg drifts, and he's slurring.
notes: Dispatch mismatch: fall dispatch, stroke-like words -> stroke keys, G.F.A.S.T. and RACE.

text: bystander says he saw him collapse on the sidewalk and start shaking all over for about a minute, now he's post-ictal, responds to voice, tongue lac on the left side, sugar 104
facts: tongue lac on the left side
notes: Witnessed collapse with seizure activity is not stroke-like: no stroke.onset_witnessed.

text: he has epilepsy, he takes keppra twice a day and he missed his dose last night. i saw the whole seizure, he went stiff and then his arms and legs were jerking, it lasted maybe two minutes
speaker: mother

text: Fifty-eight year old male, substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm since about 1400, seven out of ten, took one of his own nitro at home with no relief. Twelve lead done at 1432, monitor's reading acute MI suspected, it's transmitted to Mercy General.
facts: substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm
notes: Left arm radiation is pain, not a deficit. Transmitted-to hospital is not a stated transport destination.

text: sats 84 on room air, resps 28, she's tripoding with crackles bilaterally, put her on CPAP at 7.5 of peep, sats coming up to 93

Driver, restrained, T-boned on the driver side at about 40, moderate intrusion and fire had to extricate her. C/o left chest wall pain, crepitus to the left lateral ribs, c-collar placed. No facial droop, moves all four.
facts: t-boned on the driver side at 40
crepitus to the left lateral ribs
notes: Negative stroke screen on a trauma call gives no G.F.A.S.T. or RACE values (§4e).

text: Roommate found him in the bathroom. He's unresponsive, pinpoint pupils, resps 6, end tidal 62. Fire gave 4 of narcan intranasal before we got here, we bagged him and gave another 2 milligrams IV at 2231, now he's breathing 14 on his own.
i was walking my dog and i watched her trip on the curb and go down, she caught herself with her hands, she was talking to me the whole time
speaker: neighbor
notes: Witnessed trip-and-fall: a trauma mechanism, so no stroke.onset_witnessed (§4c).

text: Called in as a sick person. Daughter talked to her at 12:30 and she was fine, came over at three and found her in the recliner. Eyes deviated to the right, left face is flat, left arm and leg won't lift off the bed.
facts: left arm and leg won't lift off the bed
notes: Dispatch mismatch. Discovery time (three) is no time fact.

text: husband says she was normal at lunch. now she's slurring, sweaty and confused, D-stick is 31, she can't safely swallow so no oral glucose, pushing D10 now
notes: Near-miss: slurring inside a hypoglycemia presentation (glucose 31 in the same breath). §4c: stroke keys are not labeled for hypoglycemia, so no stroke.lkw, deficits or G.F.A.S.T. speech.

text: Security found him behind the loading dock, last seen normal at shift change around 2200. He's hypothermic, core temp 33.1, GCS 9, E2 V2 M5, sugar 88.
notes: Hypothermia, no stroke-like words: 'last seen normal' gives no stroke.lkw (§4c).

text: he just slid off the edge of the bed onto the floor, he's not hurt, he just can't get up by himself cause his legs are weak from the parkinsons, he takes sinemet
speaker: wife
facts: slid off the edge of the bed
slid off the edge of the bed onto the floor
notes: Chronic bilateral leg weakness from Parkinson's is not a focal stroke-like deficit: no stroke.deficits.

text: gave 324 of aspirin PO, nitro point four SL times three, pain went from an eight to a four, BP one forty two over eighty eight, heart rate 96
I can't catch my breath, it's been getting worse since yesterday, I've been coughing up green stuff and running fevers. I'm on eliquis and my inhaler.
speaker: patient
notes: 'My inhaler' is a drug class without a name: no meds.list. Fevers alone give no infection.suspected.

text: Low speed rear-end, maybe ten miles an hour, officer says the car just drifted into the back of the truck. Driver has a left facial droop, left arm drift, eyes deviated to the right, and she doesn't recognize her left arm as hers.
facts: doesn't recognize her left arm as hers
notes: Dispatch mismatch on a collision. Hedged speed dropped. Agnosia for the arm only -> RACE 1, no G.F.A.S.T. speech.

text: Witnessed by a coworker, sudden collapse then about a minute of tonic clonic activity, incontinent, now post-ictal, opens eyes to voice, moving all extremities, no known seizure history.
notes: Witnessed collapse into a seizure: not stroke-like, so no stroke.onset_witnessed; 'moving all extremities' on a non-stroke presentation gives no G.F.A.S.T.

text: he snorted something at the party like twenty minutes ago and then he just nodded off and wouldnt wake up so i gave him my narcan spray and he started breathing better
speaker: friend

text: Ninety-one year old female, mechanical fall from standing, tripped over her walker, struck the back of her head on the tile. She's on warfarin. Hematoma to the occiput, no LOC per the caregiver.
facts: mechanical fall from standing, tripped over her walker
low level fall with significant head impact

text: she stood up from the toilet and just fainted, i caught her before she hit the ground, she came around in like thirty seconds, she hasnt been eating much
speaker: husband
notes: Witnessed syncope is not a stroke onset: no stroke.onset_witnessed.

text: Sugar's 126 so it's not her sugar. She's got slurred speech, can't find her words, right arm drifts down and the right side of her mouth droops. Husband says she was normal at 1830.
facts: right side of her mouth droops
notes: Dispatch mismatch: normal glucose plus focal signs. Slurred and word-finding trouble without severity give no RACE aphasia.

text: Nurse at the facility says she's been more confused than baseline since yesterday. Temp 102.4, heart rate 118, pressure 94 over 52, foley bag has cloudy urine, probably urosepsis.

Lift assist only, found her sitting on the floor next to the recliner, says she slid down to the floor and couldn't get back up, denies hitting her head, denies pain, A and O times four, BP 128 over 76.
he takes plavics and lipiter and the metoprolol, no blood thinners, he's allergic to penicillin and sulfa
speaker: wife

text: Son found him slumped in his chair. Last known well was 0700 when they had coffee. He's got a forced gaze to the left, no movement in the right arm or right leg, and he's globally aphasic, not saying a word.
facts: no movement in the right arm or right leg
notes: Dispatch mismatch. 'Son found him' -> onset_witnessed false with the finder as source (§5b).

text: Sixty-nine yom, witnessed fall off a step stool, wife saw the whole thing, he landed on his right shoulder, no head strike. Face symmetric, no arm drift, speech is clear. Deformity to the right clavicle.
notes: Near-miss: witnessed trauma fall gives no stroke.onset_witnessed; negative stroke screen on a trauma call gives no G.F.A.S.T./RACE. No height -> no fall criterion.

text: Seventy-one year old female with COPD, on 2 liters at home, sats 86 on her 2 liters, wheezing throughout, gave a duoneb, sats up to 91, resps 24, temp 38.4, looks like pneumonia.
Twenty four year old female, per the roommate she took a handful of her zoloft about an hour ago, GCS 13, sats 97 on room air, heart rate 104.
notes: GCS 13 alone gives no ACVPU letter.

text: Post-ictal after a witnessed seizure, but twenty minutes out he still has a right facial droop and his right arm drifts, left side is strong, speech is slurred. Glucose 112.
notes: Dispatch mismatch: focal signs after a seizure are stroke-like words (§4c), labeled as said. The seizure being witnessed is not a stroke onset.

text: Rollover on the freeway, unrestrained driver, ejected, GCS 7, E1 V2 M4, open deformity left femur, obvious deformity right femur, pelvis is unstable, tourniquet on the left thigh at 1506.
facts: rollover on the freeway, unrestrained, ejected
two or more proximal long bone fractures
bleeding requiring tourniquet or wound packing

text: i havent seen her since yesterday morning, she was fine then getting her mail, her newspapers are piling up on the porch and i could see her on the kitchen floor through the window
speaker: neighbor
facts: newspapers are piling up on the porch
notes: Person-down call without stroke-like words: 'fine then' gives no stroke.lkw.

text: Twelve lead's attached, sinus tach at 112, no STEMI on the 12-lead. 18 gauge in the right AC, gave 4 of zofran IV for the nausea.
I was up on the ladder cleaning the gutters and it slipped, I fell maybe ten or twelve feet onto the driveway, my back is killing me and I can't feel my legs
speaker: patient
facts: ladder slipped, fell onto the driveway
spinal injury with new motor or sensory loss
notes: Hedged height -> no 'fall over 10 feet'. Numbness from a suspected spinal injury is not a stroke deficit (§4c).

text: Dad's a type two diabetic, he takes metformin and jardiance, his sugar was 45 when I checked it and I gave him some orange juice and a glucose gel before you got here
speaker: daughter

text: Grandson called it in as a sick person. She's eighty-eight, he says she was her normal self at 8 this morning. Now she's got left sided weakness and her smile is a little uneven, speech is clear though, and she knows her left side is weak.
notes: Dispatch mismatch. 'Left sided weakness' has no severity: G.F.A.S.T. 1, no RACE arm. Knowing the deficit but not stated about the arm -> no RACE agnosia value. 'She' is not a sex statement.

text: Four year old male, mom says he got into the peanuts at a birthday party, hives across the chest, stridor. Mom gave his EpiPen Junior at 1340, we gave epi 0.15 IM at 1352 and an albuterol neb.
Fifty yof found down in her car in the parking garage by security, unknown down time, responds to pain only, pupils equal, sugar 67, end tidal 28.
notes: Found down, no stroke-like words: no stroke.onset_witnessed.

text: Called for a fall, but daughter says it started with her words coming out all jumbled at about 1620, she was right there and saw it. Now she's aphasic, can't get a word out, face is symmetric, no drift in either arm, eyes midline.
notes: Dispatch mismatch with negatives: the presentation is stroke-like, so stated normals get their 0s. 'No drift in either arm' is arm-only -> RACE arm 0, no G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg (legs not stated).

text: No pulse, starting compressions at 0214. Fire had already given 2 of narcan IM. Pads on, asystole, IO in the left tibia.
it started around two while I was mowing the lawn, it feels like an elephant sitting on my chest. I already took a baby aspirin. I'm allergic to morphine.
speaker: patient
notes: Patient's own aspirin before the call is meds.list, not meds.given.

text: the motorcycle hit the car and he flew over the handlebars and landed like fifteen feet away, he wasnt moving for a bit, he had his helmet on
speaker: bystander
facts: motorcycle hit the car, flew over the handlebars

text: Okay, family says she was fine yesterday, we'll get more history on the way. Let's get her on the stair chair.

Found down in the hallway by group home staff, the aide says she was fine at 0530 at med pass. Left gaze deviation, right face droops a little, can't hold her right arm up at all, and she's mumbling nonsense.
facts: can't hold her right arm up at all
notes: Dispatch mismatch. Nonsense speech with no severity: G.F.A.S.T. speech 1, no RACE aphasia (§5b).

text: he had one of his seizures, he's on dilantin and depakote, the neurologist just upped the dose last week, he doesn't take any blood thinners
speaker: wife

text: Thirty-one weeks pregnant, G2P1, short of breath since about 3 this afternoon, sats 95 on room air, resps 22, BP 156 over 102, heart rate 108.
she was fine when i talked to her at seven last night, this morning i found her on the floor and the whole right side of her face is drooping and she cant move her right arm
speaker: son
facts: whole right side of her face is drooping
notes: Dispatch mismatch on the other mic: family description gives deficits only, no G.F.A.S.T./RACE (§5b); stroke-like words in the same utterance make the LKW and 'found' count.

text: BGL just reads HI on the glucometer, she's been peeing a lot and vomiting since last night, breath smells fruity, resps 30 and deep, heart rate 124.
notes: Glucometer HI gives no numeric glucose (§5b).

text: Frequent flyer for lift assists. She's at her baseline per the caregiver, moves all four extremities equally, no complaints, we got her back into bed.
notes: Negative motor finding on a non-stroke presentation: no G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg.
